messages.subject: Structural regression in bifactor model
parts:
I am fitting a bifactor model with orthogonal factors. In a later stage, I want to do an exploratory analysis in which variable Y is regressed on different factors in this bifactor model. See example below:

bifactormodel<-'
F1=~x1+x2+x3
F2=~x4+x5+x6
GenF=~x1+x2+x3+x4+x5+x6

F1~~0*F2
F1~~0*GenF
F2~~0*GenF'

regmodel<-'
F1=~x1+x2+x3
F2=~x4+x5+x6
GenF=~x1+x2+x3+x4+x5+x6

Y~F1+F2+GenF'

Do I need to add covariance terms for the factors to account for possible shared variance among factors in the regression? Like this:

regmodel<-'
F1=~x1+x2+x3
F2=~x4+x5+x6
GenF=~x1+x2+x3+x4+x5+x6

Y~F1+F2+GenF

F1~~F2
F1~~GenF
F2~~GenF'

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Structural regression in bifactor model
parts:
Matti

The general factor must be uncorrelated to the other factors. But the other factors most commonly are correlated between them.

F1~~NA*F2 ## estimate this covariance
F1~~0*GenF
F2~~0*GenF


And keep those for regression models
